subject: Sustained token/sec & QPS MAP — performance readout and unit econ finalization
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.com>
To: Tom Raines <tom.r@ledgerco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.b@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.j@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP: sustained throughput evaluation + unit economics (see attached)

Tom — attaching the MAP draft and the perf evaluation plan we talked about. Outline below, looking for OK to run the sustained window next week. Key items: 

1) Objectives
- Validate sustained throughput (tokens/sec) for your 1k-concurrent billing profile
- Measure TTFT (time-to-first-token) and streaming per-token latency at 95/99p
- Produce realistic unit-econ (cost-per-1M tokens) for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Caching-enabled Dedicated

2) Test matrix (environments / variants)
- Env A: Redwood Dedicated (4xA100-40GB), no KV cache, quant=fp16
- Env B: Dedicated + KV prefix caching (50% cache hit sim)
- Env C: Hosted baseline (our standard prod config)
- Workload: avg prompt 120 tokens, avg completion 80 tokens -> 200 tokens/request; synthetic mix: 60% short (<=50), 30% medium (200), 10% long ( >=600)

3) Acceptance criteria (MAP gates)
- Sustained window (90m) tokens/sec >= 10k aggregate across cluster AND 95p TTFT <= 250ms
- Per-request 99p latency < 1.2s for median-sized completions
- Unit econ: Dedicated+cache target <= 40% of Hosted cost per 1M tokens

4) Schedule (proposed)
- 2027-09-10: canary run (30m)
- 2027-09-10: sustained window (90m)
- 2027-09-11: analysis and unit-econ draft
- 2027-09-12: MAP sign-off and mutual action plan close

If this looks good I’ll schedule the canary for Friday morning and share the test harness details (client bootstrap, concurrency ramp script). Attachments: MAP v1.2, test harness config.

Cheers,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.f@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: map-20270909-MAP-v1.2.pdf (PDF, 48KB), test-harness-config.yaml (text)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.b@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.com>, Tom Raines <tom.r@ledgerco.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.j@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: sustained throughput evaluation + unit economics (see attached)

Tom / Naomi — ran the canary + sustained window on 2027-09-10 (logs attached). Summary of the canonical sustained run (Env A/B/C as Naomi defined):

Test configuration (canonical): 4xA100-40GB (Dedicated), 520 simulated concurrent sessions, avg tokens/request=200, 90m sustained window, 15 min warmup.

Results (aggregated):
- Env A (Dedicated, no cache):
  - Aggregate sustained tokens/sec: 13,200 tok/s (stable 90m window)
  - Approx tokens/sec per GPU: ~3,300 tok/s
  - Sustained QPS (requests/sec): ~66 req/s (13,200 / 200)
  - Median TTFT: 92 ms; p95 TTFT: 215 ms; p99 TTFT: 420 ms
  - Per-token streaming latency: ~7.2 ms/token during steady state
  - GPU utilization: 72% avg; memory headroom ~9–11GB

- Env B (Dedicated + KV cache sim, 50% hit):
  - Aggregate sustained tokens/sec: 18,400 tok/s (effective, due to cache re-use)
  - Sustained QPS: ~92 req/s
  - Median TTFT: 68 ms; p95 TTFT: 140 ms; p99 TTFT: 260 ms
  - Observed tail reduction primarily on p95/p99 for TTFT (cache avoids model compute on prefix-heavy requests)

- Env C (Hosted baseline):
  - Aggregate sustained tokens/sec: 8,500 tok/s (our prod config under same workload)
  - Sustained QPS: ~42 req/s
  - Median TTFT: 120 ms; p95 TTFT: 320 ms

Unit economics (back-of-envelope from the run + infra amortization model):
- Hosted (per 1M tokens): $480 USD (includes service margin, multi-tenant overhead, tracing ingestion)
- Dedicated (4xA100 amortized, no cache): $120 USD per 1M tokens (includes reserved GPU + infra + support allocation)
- Dedicated + KV caching (50% effective hit for this workload): $48 USD per 1M tokens (effective marginal compute fall-through + storage)

Notes / caveats:
- Token mix matters a lot: workloads with higher prefix reuse will see cache benefits >50% in practice.
- Our Dedicated numbers assume monthly reserved commit and realistic GPU utilization across the billing window; peak-only use cases will change the math.
- Network egress from customer nodes added ~18–60ms depending on region — we observed slightly higher TTFT for EU egress in a parallel run.

Attached: sustained-run-20270910-log.csv (90m window detailed timeseries), unit-econ-calcs-20270911.xlsx (calcs + amortization assumptions).

Next steps: Naomi — can you pull these results into the MAP doc and (1) update the acceptance row for unit economics, and (2) confirm sign-off cadence? If LedgerCo signs the MAP by 2027-09-12 we’ll provide a PO template and rollout plan.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.com>
To: Tom Raines <tom.r@ledgerco.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.b@redwood.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.j@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: sustained throughput evaluation + unit economics (see attached)

Tom — thanks for the quick turn on the canary and the sustained run. I updated the MAP (v1.2 attached) with the run numbers Dylan posted and lowered the Dedicated+cache acceptance gate to: Dedicated+cache cost <= 40% of Hosted per 1M tokens AND p95 TTFT <= 200ms (adjusted to reflect measured 140ms).

Action items to close MAP: 
- LedgerCo: confirm PO cadence by EOD 2027-09-13 (Tom)
- Redwood: produce final Bill of Materials + provisioning ticket once PO is received (Naomi)
- Joint: schedule first-week rollout validation window (15–30 minute daily checks for first 5 days)

Tom — does the p95 TTFT target change your internal acceptance? If not, I’ll move this MAP to "Ready for Exec Sign-off" and route to Finance for the PO paperwork.

Best,
Naomi
_internal_summary: MAP thread: canary + 90m sustained run produced 13.2k tok/s (no-cache), 18.4k tok/s (50% cache). Unit econ: Hosted $480/1M, Dedicated $120/1M, Dedicated+cache $48/1M. MAP updated and awaiting LedgerCo PO by 2027-09-13 for sign-off.
